correctness.rationale: A separately written exact Q(sqrt(5)) check obtains the facet supports and the sixty pentagon–triangle edge incidences and sweeps consecutive intersections on each normal circle. Each open arc has exactly one zero among the sixteen circle coordinates; extending its sign in both ways gives adjacent chambers, and every full-dimensional sign cone has boundary arcs. This independent sweep gives 90 rays (60 double, 30 quadruple), 240 arcs and 152 cells, with angle/size classes of multiplicities 12,20,60,60 and refined adjacency 60,60,120. It also checks equal pentagon sides in addition to equal angles. An edge with opposite incident facet signs is exposed by a positive combination of its two normals perpendicular to the view direction. Genericity prevents collapsed edges and prevents a lifted support line from exposing a facet, so these edges count the projected polygon edges and vertices exactly. The angles give the stated areas by spherical excess, using cos(beta+eta)=−cos(2 gamma) with beta+eta and pi−2 gamma in (0,pi); division by 4pi gives the stated Haar law. Intersection multiplicities count distinct circles, whereas silhouette signs use all 32 outward facet normals.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker prints the adjacency histograms rather than asserting their exact values; the independent sweep asserts them. Nongeneric views are not classified.

evidence: The polar of the regular icosidodecahedron is the rhombic triacontahedron. Taking the polar within the projection plane identifies the projection with the polar of the corresponding central section, preserving the number of sides. The sixteen planes through dual vertices' orthogonal complements are therefore the same normal-circle arrangement.
The dodecahedral same-day record has the exact same ten-gon probability but a different 92-chamber split; the icosahedral central-section record has six normal circles.

Other Platonic section records match at most some subarrangement geometry or marginal values, not the labelled sixteen-circle atlas. The same-day date does not settle order.

value.rationale: For a canonical Archimedean solid the atlas specifies both which generic views give each silhouette size and exactly which classes can occur across a single generic boundary. The exact counts and angles resolve the split between the two dodecagonal regions and the absence of direct ten-to-fourteen transitions, information not recoverable from a mean or one marginal. This is a reproducible natural viewing invariant with an explicit dual section interpretation, not a one-off numerical view.
residual_risks: Orthographic generic views of this one solid only; no nongeneric or perspective atlas is claimed.
